newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweet crude grades gain on move from WTI spot.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweet crude grades gain on move from WTI spot.

text.p: U.S. crude grades found favor against outright barrels Wednesday afternoon, pushing sweet and sour diferentials to firmer price levels.
"People are thinking June/July will be weak, so grades have gained. There are a lack of foreigns available, even for June, sweet cargoes have dried up," said a Texas cash trader.
May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was currently around steady to five cents off the June WTI at $19.45-55 a barrel, around 10 cts lower than late Tuesday clockings.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked out to 10-15 cts over the benchmark, 20 cts better than late Tuesday.
May West Texas Sour/Midland was pegged at a $1.45-55 discount to the marker, with Eugene Island last done at $1.40 under the WTI, traders said.
The May/June roll was sold at numbers below the even mark, but has been steady from late Tuesday.
Grades have also benefitted from sentiment the WTI market is well-supplied.
"There is plenty of oil, and people are looking to get back to grades," said a trader.
Other grade talk had Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire selling at wide numbers, including a deal at 80 cts under the marker.
Midland/WTI was done weaker at WTI/Cushing -39 cts.
